reason: Slice 1 of TB-48: every write of a protected config file (first default from the configurator or the daemon, save, resolved save, acknowledged overwrite) first keeps a private (0700/0600), verified, durable generation of what it replaces (the absence and whether its directory existed, or the exact bytes and permission bits, also of an invalid personal file) in $XDG_STATE_HOME/touchbar-customizer/backups (absolute) or $HOME/.local/state/...; the saved file keeps its bits, a new one is 0600. Reads, validation failures and conflicts found before the generation is published keep nothing; unchanged saves reuse the newest verified generation; generations are never deleted, outlive the process and are listed per config. Symlinked (dangling or not), hard-linked, FIFO, socket and directory config paths, and untrusted stores (open mode, symlinked or swapped backups dir, inside the config directory a restore replaces, a file, unwritable, no room: EFBIG) are refused before any mutation with the original intact and a retry succeeding; damaged generations (edited data, garbled manifest, data symlink) are never verified, reused or deleted; crash leftovers are ignored and kept; concurrent writers in threads or processes lose no version and get unique ids. Both binaries are wired through their production entry with isolated HOME/XDG_STATE_HOME; try-app.sh and rehearsal run give both apps one private store and never touch the caller's state; no Rust test that starts a product binary leaks into the caller's XDG_STATE_HOME (runtime decoy). Integration amendment (with TB-46 save receipts): the rehearsal-run isolation double is a faithful configurator and daemon (generation before every write, receipts, symlink refusal), so the run reaches both binaries by its ordinary route; the check fails if the daemon does not run, and proves the profile HOME and an unhanded, unchanged caller XDG_STATE_HOME decoy from the generations on disk. Late-conflict amendment (ADR-0015): when the last check finds a change after the generation was published, a save or acknowledged overwrite is refused as ChangedAfterKeep (file changed) or RefusedAfterKeep (path made unsafe) naming the retained id: the other editor's file or link is not replaced, the retained generation stays verified and listed holding exactly what the write would have replaced, the attempt is no success, and a retry from the file on disk succeeds; the configurator keeps the draft and both conflict resolutions, names the id and lists it, and its Overwrite then succeeds.
